exposure: mode of delivery (routine cesarean delivery, cesarean hysterectomy, bleeding after cesarean delivery, bleeding after vaginal delivery)
outcome: reinfusion of intraoperative blood salvage blood
volume of reinfused shed blood units
cohort: Obstetric patients experiencing hemorrhage who underwent intraoperative blood salvage at a regional tertiary care maternity hospital over an eight-year period.
finding: Only 21% of obstetric hemorrhage patients who utilized intraoperative blood salvage received a reinfusion of their own blood, with patients undergoing cesarean hysterectomy or experiencing significant bleeding (after cesarean or vaginal delivery) being most likely to receive a reinfusion.
mod_finding: While intraoperative blood salvage was most common in routine cesarean deliveries, only 13% of these patients received a reinfusion, compared to 73% for cesarean hysterectomy, 69% for bleeding after cesarean, and 53% for bleeding after vaginal delivery.
